title: The Return of Christ
summary: The blessed hope of the church: the certainty and manner of Christ's return, the signs of the end, the rapture and tribulation, the millennium, and how to live ready.
description: "This same Jesus... shall so come in like manner" (Acts 1:11). This course studies what the Bible teaches about the second coming: its certainty and manner, the signs Jesus gave, the antichrist and the great tribulation, the different views of the rapture and the millennium held by Bible-believing Christians (each presented fairly), and the call to watchfulness, holiness and mission while we wait.
objectives: Establish the certainty and manner of Christ's return
Study the signs of the end in Matthew 24 and elsewhere
Explain the antichrist and the great tribulation
Present fairly the views on the rapture and the millennium
Apply the blessed hope to daily living
outcomes: Describe Christ's return as personal, visible and sudden
Explain the signs Jesus gave and warn against date-setting
Compare pre-, mid- and post-tribulation views
Compare premillennial, amillennial and postmillennial views
Show how hope of Christ's return produces holiness and mission

modules.title: He Is Coming Again
modules.intro: The return of Christ is one of the most often repeated promises in Scripture. This week we study its certainty and manner.

lessons.title: The promise
lessons.body:
Jesus promised, "if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself" (John 14:3). At His ascension angels said, "this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven" (Acts 1:11).

The New Testament mentions His return hundreds of times. It is "that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ" (Titus 2:13).

Scoffers will say, "Where is the promise of his coming?" But "The Lord is not slack concerning his promise"; He is patient, giving time for repentance (2 Peter 3:4, 9).

lessons.title: Personal, visible and glorious
lessons.body:
Christ's return will be:

- **Personal**: "the Lord himself shall descend from heaven" (1 Thessalonians 4:16). Not merely a spiritual influence or the coming of the Spirit.
- **Visible**: "every eye shall see him" (Revelation 1:7). "As the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west" (Matthew 24:27).
- **Glorious**: "in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory" (Matthew 24:30), with His angels (25:31).
- **Bodily**: "in like manner" as He ascended (Acts 1:11).

This rules out claims that Christ has already returned secretly or in some person (Matthew 24:23-26).

lessons.title: Sudden and unknown
lessons.body:
"But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only" (Matthew 24:36). He will come "as a thief in the night" (1 Thessalonians 5:2), "in such an hour as ye think not" (Matthew 24:44).

As in Noah's day, people will be eating, drinking and marrying, unaware, until judgment comes (24:37-39).

This rules out **date-setting**. Many have predicted dates and been proved wrong, bringing shame on the gospel. Our task is not to calculate but to be ready.

terms.def: Christ's personal, visible return in glory.
Greek for 'coming' or 'presence', used of Christ's return.
Paul's name for the glorious appearing of Christ (Titus 2:13).
The study of the last things: death, Christ's return, judgment and the new creation.
A picture of the unexpectedness of Christ's return.
Predicting the time of Christ's return, which Scripture forbids.

texts.teaches: I will come again and receive you unto myself.
This same Jesus shall come in like manner as He went.
Look for the blessed hope and glorious appearing of Christ.
Every eye shall see Him.
No one knows the day and hour but the Father.

summary: Christ's return is certain and often promised.
It will be personal, visible, bodily and glorious.
No one knows the day or hour; date-setting is forbidden.
God's patience gives time for repentance.

questions.q: What does Titus 2:13 call Christ's return?
Who knows the day and hour of Christ's return?
Why is the Lord delaying His coming, according to 2 Peter 3:9?
options: He is patient, wanting all to repent

questions.q: What does parousia mean?

modules.title: Signs of the End
modules.intro: Jesus gave signs to watch for, not to calculate dates. This week we study Matthew 24 and other passages.

lessons.title: The Olivet discourse
lessons.body:
Jesus' disciples asked, "what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?" (Matthew 24:3). He spoke of:

- False christs and deception (24:4-5, 24).
- Wars and rumours of wars, famines, pestilences and earthquakes: "the beginning of sorrows" (24:6-8).
- Persecution of believers and many falling away (24:9-10).
- Lawlessness and love growing cold (24:12).
- The gospel preached "in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come" (24:14).

Some of this was fulfilled in AD 70, when Jerusalem fell (24:2); much awaits final fulfilment.

lessons.title: Perilous times
lessons.body:
Paul warned that "in the last days perilous times shall come": people will be "lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud... lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof" (2 Timothy 3:1-5).

He also warned of departure from the faith: "some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils" (1 Timothy 4:1), and of people who "will not endure sound doctrine" (2 Timothy 4:3).

The "last days" began with Christ's first coming (Hebrews 1:2; Acts 2:17). We have lived in them ever since, and these conditions will intensify.

lessons.title: Israel and the nations
lessons.body:
Paul taught that "blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved" (Romans 11:25-26). Many believe this points to a future turning of many Jewish people to Christ.

Zechariah foresaw that "they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him" (Zechariah 12:10).

Christians differ on the prophetic significance of the modern state of Israel (founded in 1948). Dispensationalists see it as a key sign; others are more cautious. All should pray for Jewish people to come to Christ (Romans 10:1) and avoid hatred of any nation.

terms.def: Jesus' teaching on the Mount of Olives about the end (Matthew 24-25).
Early birth pains such as wars and famines, not the end itself.
The period from Christ's first coming to His return.
Difficult, dangerous times marked by godlessness (2 Timothy 3:1).
The full number of Gentiles coming to faith (Romans 11:25).
A desecration of the holy place foretold by Daniel and Jesus (Matthew 24:15).

texts.teaches: Wars and rumours of wars must come, but the end is not yet.
The gospel will be preached to all nations, and then the end will come.
In the last days perilous times shall come.
And so all Israel shall be saved.
God has spoken in these last days by His Son.

summary: Jesus warned of deception, wars, persecution and lawlessness.
The gospel must be preached to all nations before the end.
The last days began with Christ's first coming and will intensify.
Many expect a future turning of Israel to Christ.

questions.q: What did Jesus call wars, famines and earthquakes?
What must happen before the end, according to Matthew 24:14?
options: The gospel preached to all nations

questions.q: When did the last days begin?
Where did Jesus give His teaching on the end?

modules.title: The Antichrist and the Tribulation
modules.intro: Scripture warns of a final opponent and a time of great trouble. This week we study the antichrist and the great tribulation.

lessons.title: Antichrist and the man of sin
lessons.body:
John wrote, "ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists" (1 John 2:18). Anyone who "denieth the Father and the Son" has the spirit of antichrist (2:22).

Paul described a final "man of sin... the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God" (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). He will come "after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders" (2:9), but the Lord "shall consume [him] with the spirit of his mouth" (2:8).

Revelation 13 describes a beast from the sea and a false prophet who demand worship and impose the mark of the beast (13:16-17).

lessons.title: The great tribulation
lessons.body:
Jesus spoke of "great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world" (Matthew 24:21). Daniel foresaw "a time of trouble, such as never was" (Daniel 12:1). Revelation describes seals, trumpets and bowls of judgment poured on a rebellious world (chapters 6-16).

Many link this to Daniel's "seventieth week" (Daniel 9:27), a seven-year period, though interpreters differ.

Interpreters read Revelation in different ways: as mostly future (**futurist**), as fulfilled in the early centuries (**preterist**), as unfolding through church history (**historicist**), or as timeless symbols of the conflict between Christ and evil (**idealist**). Many combine these.

lessons.title: The mark of the beast
lessons.body:
The beast causes all "to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark" (Revelation 13:16-17). Those who receive it and worship the beast face God's wrath (14:9-11).

The mark stands opposite to the seal of God on His servants' foreheads (7:3; 14:1). It speaks of total allegiance.

Believers should avoid two errors: fearful speculation that every new technology or ID card is the mark, and careless indifference. Christians cannot take the mark by accident; it involves deliberate worship of the beast. Our call is faithfulness to Christ whatever the cost (Revelation 12:11).

terms.def: One who opposes Christ; also the final great opponent before Christ's return.
Paul's name for the final lawless one (2 Thessalonians 2:3).
A time of unequalled distress before Christ's return.
The final 'seven' of Daniel 9:27, often taken as a seven-year tribulation.
The sign of allegiance to the beast, required to buy and sell (Revelation 13:17).

texts.teaches: Antichrist shall come, and even now there are many antichrists.
The man of sin will be revealed before the day of Christ.
The Lord will consume the wicked one with the spirit of His mouth.
There shall be great tribulation such as never was.
No one may buy or sell without the mark of the beast.

summary: Many antichrists exist now; a final man of sin will come.
Christ will destroy the antichrist at His coming.
A great tribulation will precede the end.
The mark of the beast is deliberate allegiance; believers must stay faithful.

questions.q: What did John say about antichrists in his day?
How will the man of sin be destroyed?
options: By the spirit of the Lord's mouth

questions.q: Which approach reads Revelation as mostly future?
What is the opposite of the mark of the beast?

modules.title: Views of the Rapture and Millennium
modules.intro: Bible-believing Christians hold different views on the order of end-time events. This week we present them fairly.

lessons.title: The rapture
lessons.body:
1 Thessalonians 4:17 says living believers will be "caught up" (Latin *rapiemur*, from which we get "rapture") to meet the Lord in the air. Christians differ on when this happens:

- **Pre-tribulation**: Christ comes for His church before the tribulation, then returns with His saints after it. Held by many Pentecostals, Deeper Life Bible Church and dispensationalists. They cite 1 Thessalonians 1:10, 5:9 and Revelation 3:10.
- **Mid-tribulation** or **pre-wrath**: the church is caught up during the tribulation, before God's wrath is poured out.
- **Post-tribulation**: the church goes through the tribulation and is caught up to meet Christ as He returns. Held by many Reformed and some Baptist Christians. They cite Matthew 24:29-31.

lessons.title: The millennium
lessons.body:
Revelation 20:1-6 speaks of Satan bound and saints reigning with Christ "a thousand years". Three main views:

- **Premillennialism**: Christ returns *before* a literal thousand-year reign on earth. Held by many Baptists, Pentecostals, Deeper Life and the early church fathers such as Irenaeus.
- **Amillennialism**: the thousand years is symbolic of the present age, in which Christ reigns from heaven and Satan is restrained; Christ's return ends history. Held by many Reformed, Anglican and Catholic Christians and by Augustine.
- **Postmillennialism**: the gospel will gradually transform the world into a long era of righteousness, *after* which Christ returns. Held by many Puritans and nineteenth-century missionaries.

lessons.title: Agreeing on what matters
lessons.body:
These debates involve sincere believers who love Scripture. Prophetic passages contain symbols, and wise interpreters hold their views with humility.

All orthodox Christians agree:

1. Christ will return personally, visibly and gloriously.
2. The dead will be raised.
3. All will be judged.
4. The wicked will be punished and the righteous will live with God for ever.
5. God will make all things new.

The Apostles' Creed confesses simply, "He shall come to judge the quick and the dead." Let the end-times debate never divide churches or distract from mission.

terms.def: The catching up of living believers to meet Christ (1 Thessalonians 4:17).
The view that the rapture comes before the tribulation.
The view that believers go through the tribulation and are caught up at Christ's return.
The view that Christ returns before a thousand-year reign on earth.
The view that the thousand years symbolise the present age of Christ's reign.
The view that Christ returns after a long era of gospel triumph.

summary: Rapture views: pre-, mid- (pre-wrath) and post-tribulation.
Millennial views: premillennial, amillennial and postmillennial.
Deeper Life and many Pentecostals hold pre-tribulation premillennialism.
All orthodox Christians agree on Christ's return, resurrection, judgment and new creation.

Which view holds the church is caught up before the tribulation?
Which church father is associated with amillennialism?
What do all orthodox Christians agree on?
options: Christ will return visibly to judge

modules.title: Ready for His Coming
modules.intro: The Bible teaches the second coming to change how we live now. This week we study watchfulness, holiness and mission.

lessons.title: Watch and be ready
lessons.body:
Jesus told parables to teach readiness.

- **The ten virgins** (Matthew 25:1-13): five were wise and had oil; five were foolish and were shut out. "Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour."
- **The faithful servant** (24:45-51): blessed is the servant found doing his master's work when he comes.
- **The talents** (25:14-30): each must use what the master entrusted.

Readiness is not anxious watching of the sky but faithful living. "Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning" (Luke 12:35).

lessons.title: Holiness and hope
lessons.body:
"Every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure" (1 John 3:3). "Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness" (2 Peter 3:11).

The hope of His coming also comforts the suffering: "Wherefore comfort one another with these words" (1 Thessalonians 4:18). It strengthens patience: "Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh" (James 5:8).

The Bible's last prayer is "Even so, come, Lord Jesus" (Revelation 22:20).

lessons.title: Occupy till I come
lessons.body:
In the parable of the pounds the nobleman said, "Occupy till I come" (Luke 19:13): do business with what I have given you.

When the disciples asked about the timing of the kingdom, Jesus redirected them: "It is not for you to know the times... But ye shall receive power... and ye shall be witnesses unto me" (Acts 1:7-8).

The best preparation for Christ's return is to work for Him: evangelise, make disciples, serve the poor (Matthew 25:31-46), and do our daily work faithfully. The Thessalonians who stopped working to wait for Christ were rebuked (2 Thessalonians 3:10-12).

terms.def: Living alert and ready for Christ's return.
Jesus' parable contrasting the prepared and unprepared.
Christ's instruction to work faithfully until His return (Luke 19:13).
An Aramaic prayer meaning 'Our Lord, come' (1 Corinthians 16:22).
The hope of seeing Christ that motivates holy living (1 John 3:3).
Jesus' picture of the final separation, judged by how people treated His brethren.

texts.teaches: Watch, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
Everyone with this hope purifies himself.
Live in holy conduct and godliness as you await the end.
Occupy till I come.
Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

summary: Jesus' parables call for constant readiness.
The hope of His coming produces holiness and patience.
We prepare best by faithful work and witness.
The church prays, 'Come, Lord Jesus.'

questions.q: What did the foolish virgins lack?
What does 1 John 3:3 say the hope of Christ's coming produces?
What did the nobleman tell his servants?
What is the Bible's last prayer?
options: Our Father which art in heaven

short.q: Describe the manner of Christ's return.
short.model: Personal, visible to every eye, bodily in like manner as He went, and in power and great glory.
No one knows the day or hour but the Father; Christ comes unexpectedly like a thief; our task is readiness, not calculation.

short.q: Name three signs Jesus gave in Matthew 24.
short.model: False christs and deception; wars, famines and earthquakes; persecution, lawlessness and the gospel preached to all nations.

short.q: Compare the pre-tribulation and post-tribulation views of the rapture.
short.model: Pre-tribulation: the church is caught up before the tribulation (1 Thessalonians 5:9); post-tribulation: the church goes through it and meets Christ at His return (Matthew 24:29-31).
Premillennial: Christ returns before a literal thousand-year reign; amillennial: the thousand years symbolise the present age; postmillennial: Christ returns after a long era of gospel triumph.

short.q: How should the hope of Christ's return affect daily life?
short.model: It should make us holy, watchful and patient, and keep us working and witnessing faithfully until He comes.

lists.q: List four characteristics of Christ's return.
List three parables about readiness for Christ's return.

assignments.title: End-times views compared
assignments.prompt: Present fairly the three millennial views and the main rapture views. For each, give key texts and the strongest argument. Then explain what all orthodox Christians agree on and how churches with different views can work together.

assignments.title: Living ready
assignments.prompt: Using the parables of Matthew 24-25 and at least three epistle passages, write a teaching for a youth fellowship on how to live ready for Christ's return without fear or speculation.

reading: George Eldon Ladd, The Blessed Hope
Anthony A. Hoekema, The Bible and the Future
Darrell L. Bock (ed.), Three Views on the Millennium and Beyond
